key_insight: A skew-symmetric Nitsche-augmented dual-mixed finite element scheme achieves optimal energy-norm convergence for generalized Oseen equations with mixed boundary conditions and non-solenoidal convection.
engineering_relevance: The method supports reliable finite element simulation of viscous flow with mixed boundary data and boundary layers.
method: Use an augmented pseudostress–velocity dual-mixed formulation.
Weakly impose the prescribed pseudostress normal trace through skew-symmetric Nitsche stabilization.
Prove continuous and discrete well-posedness and optimal energy-norm convergence.
evidence_signal: Two- and three-dimensional numerical experiments confirm theoretical convergence rates and evaluate performance with non-solenoidal convective fields and boundary-layer solutions.
watch_item: Optimal convergence assumes mild solution regularity; the stated stability result covers homogeneous Dirichlet conditions with general Neumann data.
paper_title: Convergence analysis of an augmented dual-mixed fnite element method with skew-symmetric Nitsche stabilization for the generalized Oseen equations with mixed boundary conditions
